f.title: Report all local drug-related safety reports (ADRs) to the Drug Office
f.statement: All certificate holders of clinical trial/medicinal test are required to report all local drug-related safety reports, i.e. reports on adverse drug reactions (ADRs), to the Drug Office.

f.title: Apply the serious adverse event/reaction definition, including medically important events
f.statement: A serious adverse event or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect. Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised for other situations such as important medical events that may jeopardize the patient or require intervention to prevent one of these outcomes; these should also usually be considered serious.

rows.actor: Holder of Certificate for Clinical Trial/Medicinal Test (sponsor)
rows.quote: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether expedited reporting is appropriate in other situations, such as important medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardize the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the definition above. These should also usually be considered serious.
rows.review_note: Review: quote covers the important-medical-event sentence; the outcome list is the preceding sentence of footnote 1 (line-break hyphen prevents quoting). Double-check: list matches source.

f.title: Submit yearly progress reports and a final study report
f.statement: Certificate holders are required to submit a progress report on a yearly basis and a final study report at the end of the study, using the attached forms for manual submission or the e-CTS webpage forms (Amendment - Category 7) for e-CTS submission. The yearly progress and final report forms include a summary of serious adverse events and whether SAEs affect the study and what action has been taken.

f.title: Submit reports via the route matching how the clinical trial certificate was issued
f.statement: Type 1(a) reports (serious unexpected ADRs) are submitted by email whether the certificate was issued manually or via e-CTS. Type 1(b) and Type 2 reports (end-of-trial ADR summary, progress and final reports) are submitted manually or by email when the certificate was issued via manual application, and via e-CTS when it was issued via e-CTS.

f.statement: For any reportable ADR involving advanced therapy products, in addition to the requirement for reporting ADRs of pharmaceutical products, clinical trial certificate holders should refer to Section 6 of the 'Guidance for Pharmaceutical Industry - Adverse Drug Reaction Reporting Requirements' for consideration.
